ud2.7:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Wood, at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
ud2.7:1.3: Then at that time a certain lay follower’s only son, who was beloved and dear, had died.
ud2.7:2.1: Then many lay followers, with wet clothes and hair, in the middle of the day went to the Fortunate One, and after going and worshipping the Fortunate One, they sat down on one side. While sat on one side the Fortunate One said this to those lay followers:
ud2.7:2.2: “Now why are you lay followers, with wet clothes and hair, coming here in the middle of the day?”
ud2.7:3.1: When that was said, that lay follower said this to the Fortunate One:
ud2.7:3.2: “My only son, who was beloved and dear, reverend Sir, has died.
ud2.7:3.3: That is why we, with wet clothes and hair, are coming here in the middle of the day.”
ud2.7:4.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud2.7:5.1: “Hosts of devas and many men are tied by the satisfaction in forms that are loved,
ud2.7:5.4: ~ they come under the power of the King of Death.
ud2.7:6.1: For sure those who are heedful day and night, give up forms that are loved -
ud2.7:6.3: They surely dig up the root of misery ~ (which is) Death’s bait, so difficult to transcend.”
